minutes.headline: Commission approved the DPW fuel station and culvert replacement 7-0 with standard conditions, after a heated fight over adding spill-plan review.
minutes.summary: Remote Conservation Commission meeting that accepted the Lake Shirley annual weed management plan including a Clipper pilot, and heard many hearings. The DPW fuel tank and culvert notice of intent was approved after long debate over whether to add review of the spill response plan. Several hearings were continued to July 15, a garage RDA was sent to a notice of intent on a 4-3 vote, and an enforcement order against Town land use at Fire Road 12 was voted.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved the DPW culvert and fuel station notice of intent 7-0 with a standard order of conditions, after an amendment on spill plan review failed.
An amendment to require review of the spill response plan before startup failed, and a separate amendment for a three-party sit-down before startup also failed.
A garage RDA at 161 Reservoir Road received a positive determination on a 4-3 vote, so a notice of intent is required.
The Commission voted 5-0 to issue the Town a cease and desist at Fire Road 12 and to restore pre-asphalt conditions.
Several hearings, including 135 Gilcrest, Townsend Harbor Road and 932 Flat Hill Road, were continued to July 15.

why_it_matters: The DPW fuel station was approved without a condition requiring review of its spill response plan, so protection of nearby wetlands rests on the standard conditions and on the plan as presented.
The cease and desist against the Town at Fire Road 12 shows that Town projects are held to the same wetlands rules as private property owners.
watch_next: The July 15 Commission meeting, where the continued hearings return.
The violation letter template, which the agent is to bring back at the next meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most motions and outcomes, including the continuances, the DPW amendment votes, and the Pleasant Street, 155 Reservoir Road and Flat Hill Road determinations. Most name and address differences are caption errors, but a few votes differ substantively: the Flat Hill continuance (ours 6-1, official 4-2), the 392 Sunset Lane recusal, and the Fire Road cease and desist, where the official gives no vote.
